title: AMD CEO Lisa Su rushes to Taiwan for more AI chip capacity
source_used: Reuters (wire text read in KELO-AM's copy), with the opening paragraph of DigiTimes and Taiwan News for context
key_facts: Reuters (Taipei, 6 Oct 2026): AMD chief executive Lisa Su told reporters AMD raised its chip supply through 2026 and will "substantially increase" it in 2027.
Su said one purpose of the Taiwan visit was to make sure AMD's supply chain can ramp up CPU and GPU production for AI demand; she had met Foxconn and was due to meet TSMC.
Su said AMD needs more advanced wafer capacity because demand will be very high for the next several years, and that AMD now plans three to five years ahead.
Asked whether TSMC had discussed a possible investment in Texas with AMD, Su did not answer directly.

Su said AMD is working closely with memory chipmakers and was going to South Korea later on Tuesday 6 Oct (Reuters); Taiwan News and BigGo, citing TechNews and CNA, put the Korea leg on Thursday 8 Oct.

DigiTimes (paywalled, opening paragraph only): Su arrived in Taiwan on 5 Oct for a lightning visit, under five months after her May trip, with no major public events but supplier meetings planned; Taiwan News and BigGo say she arrived on 6 Oct.
Taiwan News, citing TechNews: AMD's EPYC 'Venice' server processor is in mass production on TSMC's 2-nanometer process and expected to be available in 2027, with capacity said to be fully booked.
Reuters: AMD, Nvidia's closest rival in AI graphics processors, has seen its market value recently top $1 trillion.
quote_evidence: “We’ve been able to increase our supply as we’ve gone through 2026, and we’re going to substantially increase our supply in 2027,”
“There’s very, very high demand for the next several years. We can see very high demand, and so we need more advanced wafer capacity,”
AMD CEO Lisa Su arrived in Taiwan on October 5 for a lightning visit, less than five months after her May trip.
why_it_matters_hint: AMD, Nvidia's closest rival in AI processors, says its AI chip supply depends on getting more advanced manufacturing capacity, which is still scarce.
event_date: 6 Oct 2026 (Su's remarks in Taipei); DigiTimes dates her arrival 5 Oct 2026
notes: Pool item is DigiTimes (paywalled: only its opening paragraph was visible). Entry built on Reuters, read in KELO-AM's copy of the wire text, and credited to Reuters; the Reuters page was published 07:20Z on 6 Oct, shortly after the window closed, but the remarks were made earlier on 6 Oct. Outlets differ on her schedule: DigiTimes says she arrived 5 Oct; Taiwan News and BigGo say 6 Oct with a Korea leg on 8 Oct; Reuters has her leaving for Korea on 6 Oct. Our 30 Sep 2026 edition carried a DigiTimes report that she planned a South Korea trip in October.
